# core/httpsurl.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/httpsurl.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The `https://` URLs a client follows (the Location of
a redirect, or a address typed by a person) split into host, port and
path, strictly: a URL the client could be tricked by is refused, not
repaired.

What is proved: no read is out of bounds, nothing leaks, and the parts
come out as the HTTPS client needs them: a host of 1 to 255 bytes, a port
from 1 to 65535 and a path of 1 to 65535 bytes that starts with `/`. Not
proved: that the URL means to every other program what it means here. Only
the scheme `https`, a host of letters, digits, dots and hyphens (no user
information, no IPv6 literal, no percent-escapes in the host) and a path
without a space or control character (so it cannot carry a line break
into a request) are accepted; the fragment is dropped.

`import "core/httpsurl.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/num.bastio](core-num.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`httpsurl_parse`](#httpsurl_parse) | Splits an `https://` URL. |
| [`httpsurl_free`](#httpsurl_free) | Frees a parsed URL. |
| [`httpsurl_follow`](#httpsurl_follow) | The URL a redirect's `location` leads to from the server `host`:`port` (for a location that is a path starting with a single `/`, the same server) or an `https://` URL. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `HttpsUrl`

```bastio
struct HttpsUrl { host: Bytes, port: u64, path: Bytes }
```

A parsed `https://` URL.

## Functions

### `httpsurl_parse`

```bastio
fn httpsurl_parse(u: &Bytes) -> Option[HttpsUrl]
  requires blen(u) < 65536
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some.host) >= 1 && blen(result.Some.host) <= 255
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.port >= 1 && result.Some.port <= 65535
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some.path) >= 1 && blen(result.Some.path) < 65536
```

Splits an `https://` URL. `None` for another scheme, user information, an
IPv6 literal, a bad host or port, or a space or control character in the
path.

Example:

```bastio
let u = bfrom("https://Example.com:8443/a/b?q=1#top");
let mut bad = 1;
match httpsurl_parse(u) {
  Option::Some(p) => {
    if bytes_eq_str(p.host, "Example.com") && p.port == 8443 && bytes_eq_str(p.path, "/a/b?q=1") { bad = 0; }
    httpsurl_free(p);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(u);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `httpsurl_free`

```bastio
fn httpsurl_free(p: HttpsUrl)
```

Frees a parsed URL.

Example:

```bastio
let u = bfrom("https://a.example/");
match httpsurl_parse(u) {
  Option::Some(p) => { httpsurl_free(p); },
  Option::None => { bfree(u); return 1; },
}
bfree(u);
```

### `httpsurl_follow`

```bastio
fn httpsurl_follow(host: &Bytes, port: u64, location: &Bytes) -> Option[HttpsUrl]
  requires blen(host) >= 1 && blen(host) <= 255 && port >= 1 && port <= 65535 && blen(location) < 65535
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some.host) >= 1 && blen(result.Some.host) <= 255
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some.port >= 1 && result.Some.port <= 65535
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some.path) >= 1 && blen(result.Some.path) < 65536
```

The URL a redirect's `location` leads to from the server `host`:`port`
(for a location that is a path starting with a single `/`, the same
server) or an `https://` URL. `None` for anything else (another scheme, a
relative path without a leading `/`, `//host/...`).

Example:

```bastio
let loc = bfrom("/login?next=1");
let server = bfrom("example.com");
let mut bad = 1;
match httpsurl_follow(server, 8443, loc) {
  Option::Some(p) => {
    if bytes_eq_str(p.host, "example.com") && p.port == 8443 && bytes_eq_str(p.path, "/login?next=1") { bad = 0; }
    httpsurl_free(p);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(server);
bfree(loc);
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `httpsurl_host_ok`

```bastio
fn httpsurl_host_ok(u: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> bool
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(u)
  ensures result ==> to > from && to - from <= 255
```

Internal: `u[from..to]` is a host name: 1 to 255 letters, digits, dots and
hyphens.

### `httpsurl_path_ok`

```bastio
fn httpsurl_path_ok(u: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> bool
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(u)
```

Internal: `u[from..to]` has no space, control character or DEL.

### `httpsurl_find`

```bastio
fn httpsurl_find(u: &Bytes, from: u64, a: u8, b: u8, c: u8) -> u64
  requires from <= blen(u)
  ensures result >= from && result <= blen(u)
```

Internal: the first position at or after `from` of a byte in `stops`
(`n` if there is none).

### `httpsurl_path`

```bastio
fn httpsurl_path(u: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> Bytes
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(u) && to - from < 65535
  ensures blen(result) >= 1 && blen(result) < 65536
```

Internal: the path of `u[from..to]` for a request: the span itself, or
`/` for an empty one, or `/` before a span that starts with `?`.

### `httpsurl_port`

```bastio
fn httpsurl_port(u: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64) -> u64
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(u)
  ensures result <= 65535
```

Internal: the port in `u[from..to]` (`:` already dropped), 0 if it is not
1 to 65535.
